T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — BP's full strategic reset, O'Neill's delivery track record, governance stability

Synopsis:
BP has confirmed Ian Tyler as its third permanent chair in under a year, promoting him from interim role after Albert Manifold's abrupt May exit. Tyler is praised for stability and boardroom experience, but his weak performance record as Balfour Beatty CEO (13% TSR vs. 80–140% for peers) raises questions about his capacity to drive deep strategic change. The piece argues the execution burden falls squarely on CEO Meg O'Neill, who must deliver cost cuts, asset disposals, and debt reduction amid BP's ongoing pivot back to fossil fuels. Oil around $95/bbl helps cash flow but muddies performance attribution.
